analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlRemoveID` passes `attr->id->value` directly to `xmlHashRemoveEntry(...)` with `xmlFreeIDTableEntry` as the deallocator. The hash removal frees the `xmlID` object (`attr->id`) via `xmlFreeIDTableEntry/xmlFreeID`, but `xmlHashRemoveEntry` may still read the key pointer during/after removal. Because that key pointer aliases memory inside the just-freed `xmlID` (`id->value`), this creates a use-after-free inside `xmlRemoveID` itself. The bug is the unsafe lifetime/aliasing of the key argument during deletion.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the xinclude harness, attacker-controlled XML creates an `xml:id` attribute (so an ID entry is allocated via `xmlAddID*` and linked as `attr->id`). Later XInclude processing (`xmlXIncludeIncludeNode`) frees nodes/attributes, triggering `xmlFreeProp` on an ID attribute, which calls `xmlRemoveID`. Trigger requires an attribute with `atype == XML_ATTRIBUTE_ID` and a valid `attr->id` entry so that `xmlRemoveID` attempts hash removal using `attr->id->value`; during that removal the ID entry is freed and the key pointer becomes dangling, causing ASan UAF.
